drafts.title: Reduce perceived harshness on broken pavement
drafts.description: When driving over uneven or broken pavement the cabin experience should feel composed and comfortable so occupants do not describe the ride as 'harsh' or jarring.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On a standardized uneven-road route driven at 50 mph (80 km/h), average occupant-reported harshness ≤ 3 on a 0–10 scale in a 50-user trial, and peak vertical seat acceleration (95th percentile) ≤ 2.0 m/s².
assumptions: Testing follows an agreed standardized uneven-road course and a repeatable driver profile.
Current-model baseline is available for validation during development (used only for internal comparison).
uncertainties: Trade-offs between ride comfort and sporty handling may require variant tuning.
Results depend on tire choice and wheel size; acceptance assumes standard OEM tire/wheel for the tested variant.

drafts.title: Reduce distracting wind noise at highway speeds
drafts.description: At highway speeds the cabin should remain quiet and non-distracting so drivers can hold conversations and keep focus without compensating for wind noise.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: With windows closed on a highway test at 75 mph (120 km/h) in crosswind conditions representative of highway driving, interior LAeq at the driver's head position ≤ 68 dB(A) and 80%+ of participants rate wind-noise intrusion ≤ 3 on a 0–10 subjective scale in a 40-user trial.
assumptions: Measurements follow a defined microphone placement (driver head position) and repeatable wind/crosswind conditions.
Standard production exterior mirrors and sealed door/window fit for the tested vehicle.
uncertainties: Roof rails, aftermarket accessories, or open windows will change results; acceptance assumes standard configuration.
Extreme crosswinds or unusual external attachments may still generate audible noise above target.

drafts.title: Make lane-keeping assist steering smooth and predictable in curves
drafts.description: When lane-keeping assist is active the vehicle should steer through curves without abrupt corrections so drivers feel confident and not surprised by sudden steering inputs.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On a standardized winding highway route at 65–75 mph (105–120 km/h) that includes at least five medium-radius curves, 90% of drivers in a 50-user trial must report 'no abrupt steering corrections,' and objective driving-log analysis must show abrupt steering-correction events in ≤ 10% of assisted interventions.
assumptions: User trial protocol and objective event definitions are agreed and repeatable.
Trials are conducted on dry pavement and with standard driver assistance settings for highway use.
uncertainties: Behavior at the limits (poor lane markings, snow, heavy crosswind) may still require conservative interventions.
Balancing safety margin versus smoothness may require configurable sensitivity levels.

drafts.title: Find compatible fast chargers quickly during trip planning and navigation
drafts.description: While planning or on a trip the system should present only chargers compatible with the car and show real-time availability so drivers can pick and navigate to a charger confidently and quickly.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: During a simulated 200-mile trip with EV route planning, drivers can identify and start navigation to a compatible fast charger within ≤ 3 minutes in 90% of test runs; the UI explicitly shows connector type and real-time availability/occupancy for the selected charger.
assumptions: Access to up-to-date public charger metadata (connector type, power, real-time status) and navigation integration is available.
The vehicle variant is electric or plug-in hybrid and the routing algorithm supports charger compatibility filtering.
uncertainties: Data availability and accuracy from third-party charger operators may vary by region.
Some legacy chargers may lack standardized metadata, requiring fallback handling.

drafts.title: Make charge-port indicator show charging state at a glance
drafts.description: From outside the vehicle a driver should immediately know whether charging is in progress, complete, or there is a fault by looking at the charge port indicator.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: From 2 meters in daylight, 95% of test users correctly identify 'charging', 'fully charged', or 'error' within 2 seconds by viewing the charge-port indicator in a 50-user trial.
assumptions: Standard production lighting and indicator brightness are used; indicator position is visible without crouching.
Users have brief (≤5s) exposure to the indicator legend during a short familiarization.
uncertainties: Very bright sunlight or snow glare may reduce visibility; acceptance assumes typical daylight conditions.
Color-blind users may require shape or blinking patterns in addition to color; test cohort should include color vision variations.

drafts.title: Offer a powertrain variant that delivers at least 600 miles real-world range on a single tank/charge
drafts.description: Customers who prioritize long distance between fuel/stops should be able to choose a 5 Series variant that reliably covers at least 600 miles in real-world mixed driving on one tank or charge.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: At least one market-available powertrain variant demonstrates ≥ 600 miles (≈965 km) real-world range in an independent, standardized mixed-driving test route and corresponding usage profile.
assumptions: This requirement can be met by offering an appropriate powertrain (e.g., highly efficient ICE, extended-range hybrid, or future long-range electric variant).
Independent real-world testing protocol and route are agreed for validating range claims.
uncertainties: Achieving 600 miles in a purely battery-electric architecture may be infeasible in the 3–5 year horizon without significant advances; a combustion or hybrid variant may be required.
Real-world range varies with driving style, load, weather and topography; acceptance is tied to standardized test conditions.

drafts.title: Regulatory and type-approval requests (customer asks)
drafts.description: Customers explicitly requested specific type approvals and regulatory compliance (Level 3 homologation in Germany, CARB emission compliance in the US, UN R155 cybersecurity, EU battery passport). These are regulatory/type-approval asks rather than direct product behaviors.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Signal records the customer requests for the following approvals: Level 3 homologation in Germany (SCOPE-R01), CARB emission compliance in all US states (SCOPE-R03), UN R155 cybersecurity approval (SCOPE-R06), and EU battery passport compliance (SCOPE-R07).
assumptions: These items are primarily regulatory/type-approval matters that require certification and engagement with authorities.
uncertainties: Timelines, feasibility and exact certification requirements are outside the product-experience scope and depend on regulators and technical deliverables.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory/type-approval requests are out of scope for customer-facing product requirements; they require legal/approval actions rather than a product-experience specification.

drafts.title: Request for 800 V electrical architecture (engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customer requested that the car uses an 800 V electrical architecture.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Signal documents the customer's request for an 800 V architecture (SCOPE-E01).
assumptions: This is a component/architecture-level specification requested by customers and requires engineering feasibility and supplier decisions.
uncertainties: Feasibility, cost and packaging implications must be evaluated by engineering; customer signal does not address trade-offs.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering specification: customers requested a specific electrical architecture (component-level wish), which is out of scope for a customer-facing requirement.

drafts.title: Request for 22 kW onboard AC charger (engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customer requested that the onboard AC charger be upgraded to 22 kW.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Signal documents the customer's request for a 22 kW onboard charger (SCOPE-E03).
assumptions: This is a technical specification request requiring electrical and thermal design decisions.
uncertainties: Onboard charger power may be constrained by the vehicle's electrical architecture and regional grid compatibility.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering specification: customer requested a specific onboard charger rating; out of scope for customer-facing requirement.

drafts.title: Request for solid-state cells with 400 Wh/kg energy density (engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customer requested that the battery uses solid-state cells achieving ~400 Wh/kg energy density.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Signal documents the customer's request for solid-state cells at ~400 Wh/kg (SCOPE-E06).
assumptions: Solid-state cell availability, qualification and supplier readiness are uncertain within the 3–5 year horizon.
uncertainties: Material readiness, cost, and safety qualifications may prevent deployment at the requested density in the successor timeframe.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering specification: customer requested a specific battery chemistry and energy density; this is a technical ask outside customer-facing requirement scope.

drafts.title: Request for front brake-disc diameter of 395 mm (engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customer requested that the front brake discs have a diameter of 395 mm.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Signal documents the customer's request for 395 mm front brake disc diameter (SCOPE-E07).
assumptions: Brake sizing affects packaging, weight and options; feasibility depends on wheel size and braking system design.
uncertainties: Specific diameter may not be compatible with all wheel options or may require braking-system re-engineering.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering specification: customer requested a specific brake-disc size; component-level requirement is out of scope for customer-facing draft.

drafts.title: Request for a specific lidar supplier for highway assist (engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customer requested that highway assist uses a lidar sensor from a named supplier.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Signal documents the customer's request for a specific lidar supplier for highway assist (SCOPE-E08).
assumptions: Supplier selection, procurement, and integration constraints are an engineering/business decision.
Customers expressed preference for lidar but did not specify performance metrics.
uncertainties: Supplier availability, cost and system integration may prevent using the named supplier; alternative sensor strategies may be required.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering specification: request names a specific supplier/component rather than a customer-facing outcome; out of scope for product-experience requirement.
